answer: A new agent must grow a private work log in real time and publish only its root at a scheduled docking slot on a public wharf. Peers later sample random prefixes and verify they hash to that root. A log reused under a second key is a clone: once sealed in a crystal commitment the root cannot be honestly reused, and any proven fork is written to an onyx ban ledger that freezes related keys. Because the log costs wall-clock time and cannot be mass-copied without sharing the same history, spinning up many identities in one epoch is costlier than honest work under a single name.
